title: Inorganic arsenic and lead top list of foodborne chemical hazards
summary:
Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic represents a major problem, according to an analysis of foodborne chemicals.

In 2021, nine foodborne chemicals caused 6.26 million cases and 1.12 million deaths. These substances are inorganic arsenic, lead, aflatoxin B1 and M1, methylmercury, cadmium, dioxin, peanut allergy, and cassava cyanide.

Published:June 16, 2026, 12:01 am

A World Health Organization (WHO) group has urged food safety stakeholders to turn evidence into action, adding that understanding the burden of foodborne disease is only the beginning.

In a statement to mark World Food Safety Day, the WHO Alliance for Food Safety called on governments, international organizations, academic institutions, and public health agencies to work together to accelerate progress toward safer food everywhere.
